title: RB1-I680T mutation potentiates tumor growth and chemotherapy sensitivity in non-small cell lung cancer via derepressing E2F1 transcription.
authors: Zhu, Yilin; Gao, Fengyuan; Liu, Yu; Wang, Jinfu; Liu, Fanrong; Wang, Biao; Wu, Boxuan; Wang, Yue; Zhang, Yifan; Tian, Zhongxian; Mu, Ning; Zhang, Xianglin; Zhao, Xiaogang; Zhao, Yunpeng; Li, Peichao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究RB1-I680T突变通过削弱RB1-E2F1蛋白-DNA转录抑制互作促进NSCLC进展，结合蛋白对接与动力学模拟解析界面机制，虽非TF-DNA结合位点预测，但属蛋白-DNA互作机制建模，方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Retinoblastoma Transcriptional Corepressor 1 (RB1) is a critical tumor suppressor restricting the malignant progression of cancer cells. Emerging evidence indicates that RB1 mutations typically promote tumorigenesis through loss of its tumor-suppressive functions. Yet, the biological significance of mutated RB1, specifically certain rare variants, in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains elusive. Here, we first reported a rare and previously uncharacterized missense mutation in RB1, the 680th residue isoleucine replaced by threonine (RB1-I680T), in NSCLC. METHODS: To investigate the functional and mechanistic consequences of the RB1-I680T mutation in NSCLC, we first used CRISPR-Cas9 to knock out endogenous RB1 in NSCLC cells. Then, we generated cell models harboring the RB1-I680T mutation by infecting these knockout cells with lentivirus carrying either wild-type RB1 (RB1-WT) or RB1-I680T expression constructs. The biological phenotypes mediated by RB1-I680T were investigated using in vitro and in vivo experiments. The exploration of the molecular mechanism was performed primarily through co-immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, dual-luciferase reporter assays, western blot analysis, and protein docking and dynamics simulation. RESULTS: Our study demonstrated that the I680T mutation caused faster tumor growth and potentiated chemotherapy-induced tumor regression compared to RB1-WT control. Mechanistic studies illustrated that the I680T mutation in RB1 disrupted its inhibition of E2F1 transcriptional activity by weakening the physical interaction between RB1 and E2F1 in a manner dependent on conformational flexibility of RB1 pocket B domain, which is essential for sustaining the enhanced proliferation and chemosensitivity in NSCLC cells. CONCLUSION: Our findings elucidate that the I680T mutation-induced loss-of-function of RB1 simultaneously confers invasive proliferation and chemotherapeutic vulnerability to tumor cells, suggesting that RB1-I680T could serve as a predictive biomarker for chemotherapy response in NSCLC. Stratifying patients based on the RB1-I680T mutation status may enable personalized therapeutic strategies, particularly for tumors with E2F1 dysregulation.
abstract_zh: 背景：视网膜母细胞瘤转录共抑制因子1（RB1）是一种关键的肿瘤抑制因子，限制癌细胞的恶性进展。新兴证据表明，RB1突变通常通过丧失其肿瘤抑制功能来促进肿瘤发生。然而，突变型RB1（特别是某些罕见变异）在非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）中的生物学意义仍不明确。在此，我们首次报道了NSCLC中一个罕见且此前未表征的RB1错义突变，即第680位残基异亮氨酸被苏氨酸替换（RB1-I680T）。方法：为研究RB1-I680T突变在NSCLC中的功能和机制后果，我们首先使用CRISPR-Cas9敲除NSCLC细胞中的内源性RB1。随后，通过用携带野生型RB1（RB1-WT）或RB1-I680T表达构建体的慢病毒感染这些敲除细胞，生成了含有RB1-I680T突变的细胞模型。通过体外和体内实验研究了RB1-I680T介导的生物学表型。分子机制的探索主要通过免疫共沉淀、免疫荧光、双荧光素酶报告基因实验、蛋白质印迹分析以及蛋白质对接和动力学模拟进行。结果：我们的研究表明，与RB1-WT对照相比，I680T突变导致更快的肿瘤生长，并增强了化疗诱导的肿瘤消退。机制研究显示，RB1中的I680T突变通过削弱RB1与E2F1之间的物理相互作用，以依赖于RB1口袋B结构域构象灵活性的方式，破坏了其对E2F1转录活性的抑制，这对于维持NSCLC细胞中增强的增殖和化疗敏感性至关重要。结论：我们的发现阐明，I680T突变诱导的RB1功能丧失同时赋予肿瘤细胞侵袭性增殖和化疗脆弱性，提示RB1-I680T可作为NSCLC化疗反应的预测性生物标志物。基于RB1-I680T突变状态对患者进行分层，可能实现个性化治疗策略，特别是针对E2F1失调的肿瘤。
